'''Harold Basch''' ({{langx|he|הרולד בש}}; 29 November 1940 – 8 November 2018) was a professor of chemistry who specialized in [[Computational Chemistry|computational chemistry]].

==Biography==
Harold Basch<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ch.biu.ac.il/basch |title=Harold Basch, Bar-Ilan University |access-date=2018-11-08 |archive-date=2017-07-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717015510/http://ch.biu.ac.il/basch |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=VP>[https://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=33&pt=20&pid=117&level=2&cPath=33&type=1&news=3240 Remembering Former Vice President for Research Prof. Harold Basch - Bar-Ilan University]</ref> was born in 1940 in [[the Bronx]], [[New York City]]. He obtained his B.A. from [[Yeshiva University]] (1962) and his M.A. and Ph.D. from [[Columbia University]] (1966) under the supervision of [[Harry B. Gray]].
He did a postdoctoral research at [[Bell Labs|Bell Telephone Laboratories]] (1966-1968) and was a principal research scientist at
[[Ford Motor Company]] ([[Dearborn, Michigan|Dearborn]], [[Michigan]]) (1968–1971). In 1970 he joined the chemistry department at [[Bar-Ilan University]] (BIU)<ref name=chemisrty>[https://ch.biu.ac.il/ Chemistry Department, BIU]</ref><ref>[https://research.biu.ac.il/departments/chemistry/ Faculty of Exact Sciences, Department of Chemistry - BIU]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> as an associate professor and became a full professor in 1977. He lived in [[Rehovot]], was married to Julia and had 5 children.

==Administrative activities==
His involvement in academic administration began early with an appointment as chairman of the department of chemistry at BIU (1973–1976).<ref name=chemisrty></ref> As an active member of the [[Academic Senate|University's Senate]], he served on and chaired many committees. Between the years 1988 and 1990, he served as the [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the faculty of sciences and mathematics<ref>[https://esc.biu.ac.il//en Faculty of Exact Sciences, BIU]</ref> and held several tenures as a member of the executive board of the Senate.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bar-Ilan University - BIU {{!}} Israel |url=https://www.biu.ac.il/en?id=13697&pt=1&pid=6909&level=5&cPath=35,983,6909 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.biu.ac.il}}</ref> Among his others administrative activities, Basch served as the academic head of the [[Holon Institute of Technology]] (1978-1981), was a member of the [[Council for Higher Education in Israel]] (1985–1991), served on scientific grants committees of the [[Israel Science Foundation]], was a member of the scientific board of the [[Israel Inter-University Computation Center]], was appointed to the National Council for Research and Development ([[Prime Minister's Office (Israel)|Prime Minister's Office]])<ref>{{Cite news |title=National Council for Civilian Research and Development |url=https://www.gov.il/en/departments/units/molmop |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241111233929/https://www.gov.il/en/departments/units/molmop |archive-date=2024-11-11 |access-date=2025-05-21 |work=GOV.IL |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref> and was a member of the computer grants committee of [[:he:הוועדה_לתכנון_ולתקצוב|The Planning and Budgeting Committee (PBC)]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2013-03-31 |title=The Planning and Budgeting Committee |url=https://che.org.il/en/the-planning-and-budgeting-committee/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240528064807/https://che.org.il/en/the-planning-and-budgeting-committee/ |archive-date=2024-05-28 |access-date=2025-05-21 |work=המועצ |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref> During the years 2005–2011, he served as the vice president for research at [[Bar-Ilan University]].<ref name=VP></ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Team Archive - The Bar-Ilan University (BIU) Research Authority |url=https://research.biu.ac.il/team/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210117181416/https://research.biu.ac.il/team/ |archive-date=2021-01-17 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=The Bar-Ilan University (BIU) Research Authority |language=en-US |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=אוניברסיטת בר אילן |url=https://www.biu.ac.il/?id=3&pt=20&cPath=3&type=1&news=1519 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.biu.ac.il}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bar-Ilan University - BIU {{!}} Israel |url=https://www.biu.ac.il/en?id=33&pt=20&pid=4&level=1&cPath=4&type=1&news=1191 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.biu.ac.il}}</ref>

==Scientific activities==
His main research interest was in the field of [[Computational Chemistry|computational chemistry]]. Basch was a pioneer in computational [[quantum chemistry]], in developing methods and innovative applications of theoretical concepts and equations to solving problems in [[chemistry]].<ref name=researchgate>[https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/38792628_Harold_Basch Harold Basch's research works - full list of publications]</ref> Already in 1962, as a beginning graduate student at [[Columbia University]], he recognized the potential use of the computer (which then filled a whole building), in chemical research. The methods and paradigms he developed are used today in modern [[:Category:Computational chemistry software|software packages]] for the calculation of [[Molecular property|molecular properties]].<ref name="MusaevBasch2002">{{cite book|last1=Musaev|first1=Djamaladdin G.|title=Computational Modeling of Homogeneous Catalysis|last2=Basch|first2=Harold|last3=Morokuma|first3=Keiji|chapter=The N≡N Triple Bond Activation by Transition Metal Complexes|volume=25|year=2002|pages=325–361|issn=0920-4652|doi=10.1007/0-306-47718-1_13|series=Catalysis by Metal Complexes|isbn=978-1-4020-0933-4}}</ref><ref name="MusaevBasch2002b">{{cite journal|last1=Musaev|first1=Djamaladdin G.|last2=Basch|first2=Harold|last3=Morokuma|first3=Keiji|title=Theoretical Study of the Mechanism of Alkane Hydroxylation and Ethylene Epoxidation Reactions Catalyzed by Diiron Bis-oxo Complexes. The Effect of Substrate Molecules|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=124|issue=15|year=2002|pages=4135–4148|issn=0002-7863|doi=10.1021/ja0176393|pmid=11942853}}</ref><ref name="TorrentMusaev2002">{{cite journal|last1=Torrent|first1=Maricel|last2=Musaev|first2=Djamaladdin G.|last3=Basch|first3=Harold|last4=Morokuma|first4=Keiji|title=Computational studies of reaction mechanisms of methane monooxygenase and ribonucleotide reductase|journal=Journal of Computational Chemistry|volume=23|issue=1|year=2002|pages=59–76|issn=0192-8651|doi=10.1002/jcc.1157|pmid=11913390|s2cid=24420102}}</ref> The list of applications he has been involved in include electron, electronic and [[Photoemission spectroscopy|photoelectronic spectroscopies]], energetics, [[Molecular geometry|geometric]] and [[Electronic structure|electronic structures]], [[chemical reaction]] paths, intermediates, and [[Transition state|transition states]], [[Ligand#Metal–ligand_multiple_bond|metal-ligand]], metal-metal, metal [[Cluster chemistry|cluster bonding]], and [[active site]] reactions in [[Metalloprotein#Metalloenzymes|metalloenzymes]].<ref name="BaschRatner2003">{{cite journal|last1=Basch|first1=Harold|last2=Ratner|first2=Mark A.|title=Binding at molecule/gold transport interfaces. I. Geometry and bonding|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=119|issue=22|year=2003|pages=11926–11942|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.1613941|bibcode=2003JChPh.11911926B}}</ref><ref name="BaschRatner2003b">{{cite journal|last1=Basch|first1=Harold|last2=Ratner|first2=Mark A.|title=Binding at molecule/gold transport interfaces. II. Orbitals and density of states|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=119|issue=22|year=2003|pages=11943–11950|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.1613942|bibcode=2003JChPh.11911943B}}</ref><ref name="BaschRatner2004">{{cite journal|last1=Basch|first1=Harold|last2=Ratner|first2=Mark A.|title=Molecular binding at gold transport interfaces. III. Field dependence of electronic properties|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=120|issue=12|year=2004|pages=5761–5770|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.1650293|pmid=15267455|bibcode=2004JChPh.120.5761B}}</ref><ref name="BaschRatner2004b">{{cite journal|last1=Basch|first1=Harold|last2=Ratner|first2=Mark A.|title=Molecular binding at gold transport interfaces. IV. Thiol chemisorption|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=120|issue=12|year=2004|pages=5771–5780|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.1650294|pmid=15267456|bibcode=2004JChPh.120.5771B}}</ref><ref name="BaschRatner2005">{{cite journal|last1=Basch|first1=Harold|last2=Ratner|first2=Mark A.|title=Binding at molecule/gold transport interfaces. V. Comparison of different metals and molecular bridges|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics|volume=123|issue=23|year=2005|pages=234704|issn=0021-9606|doi=10.1063/1.1947747|pmid=16392941|bibcode=2005JChPh.123w4704B}}</ref> The theoretical methods include single and multi-configuration [[molecular orbital theory]], [[valence bond theory]], and effective [[Core charge|core]] and [[Effective Fragment Potential Method|effective fragment potentials]].
His latest research efforts were directed towards finding appropriate molecular [[Bridged compounds|bridges]] that can serve as [[Conductive polymer|nano-conducting]] and switching elements in [[molecular electronics]].<ref name=researchgate></ref> 

During his career, Basch published more than 180 papers and book chapters.<ref name=researchgate></ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://research.biu.ac.il/researcher/professor-harold-basch/ |title=Prof. Harold Basch - Research Authority, BIU |access-date=2018-11-08 |archive-date=2018-11-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181109070719/https://research.biu.ac.il/researcher/professor-harold-basch/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://dblp.uni-trier.de/pers/hd/b/Basch:Harold dblp computer science bibliography]</ref>
